Parallel cell metadata reports actual parallel use, two subagents, timed-out process, and passing solution quality.
Parallel status records the active timeout, aborted prompt outcome, protocol validation with AgentSwarm use, artifact list, and completed official pass.
Official evaluation summary reports completed evaluation with solution_passed true and reward 1.0.

Session index maps the parallel session id to the /workspace working directory.
Test-suite child wrote focused pytest files, iterated many failures, and was interrupted during a final pytest run.
Scaffolding child wrote root files, documentation, and many examples before cancellation interrupted remaining feature-example work.
Parent fetched and installed ydata-profiling source, patched minification, smoke-tested core behavior, delegated two child scopes, and timed out with both children aborted.

direct_file_reviews.summary: Same ydata-profiling project specification as the parallel run, confirmed by matching prompt hash and byte comparison.
Serial cell metadata reports no parallel use, no subagents, normal completion, and passing solution quality.
Serial status records a completed prompt event, no delegation, artifact list, remaining budget, and completed official pass.
Official evaluation summary reports completed evaluation with solution_passed true and reward 1.0.

timeline_reviews.summary: Server event stream contains transport accounting only; no semantic task actions were projected from it.
Session index maps the serial session id to the /workspace working directory.
Single actor identified v4.17.0 as matching the dependency spec, installed it, ran smoke, upstream unit, issue, and wheel checks, then reported completion.

parallel.requirements: The parallel parent recognized a complete ydata-profiling package with pandas/pyspark-related modules, pyproject metadata, CLI, report exports, examples, docs, and tests.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent first owned core package reconstruction and smoke checks itself, then split remaining work into two children: one for pytest coverage and one for docs/examples/scaffolding.
parallel.implementation: The parent copied a ydata-profiling wheel source tree, patched htmlmin to minify_html fallback, wrote packaging files, installed editable, and verified core ProfileReport, compare, CLI, and optional dependency behavior.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Children wrote directly into the same /workspace tree for tests and docs/examples while the parent waited on AgentSwarm; the saved artifact included source, tests, docs, and many examples.
parallel.verification: The parent ran smoke tests and CLI checks before delegation; child agent-0 iterated a generated pytest suite but its final full pytest command was interrupted during cancellation.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with prompt_outcome.success false and both children reported aborted, so final child summaries and a parent final response were missing even though official evaluation passed.

serial.requirements: The serial actor recognized the task as reconstructing ydata-profiling and tied the dependency pins to the upstream v4.17.0 project.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned source copy, package metadata, install, tests, examples, wheel verification, and final reporting without delegation.
serial.implementation: It downloaded/extracted v4.17.0, copied ydata_profiling and pandas_profiling into src, wrote pyproject, MANIFEST, LICENSE, README, tests/data/examples, and installed the package.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial run assembled one coherent workspace, kept source/package metadata together, and copied official tests and data before final verification.
serial.verification: It ran smoke checks, 2135 upstream unit tests, 41 issue regression tests, targeted workspace tests, CLI help, and a wheel package-data check.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial process completed normally with a final summary; no unfinished implementation or coordination lifecycle gap is visible.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same broad project requirements and also created docs, examples, tests, and package metadata around the core source tree.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and used the dependency pins to select v4.17.0 as the matching upstream implementation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both covered the official tested package obligations; parallel added more generated scaffolding, while serial leaned on upstream tests/data rather than broad generated docs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent retained core source/setup ownership and delegated test-suite work to agent-0 and docs/examples/scaffolding to agent-1.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one actor for all work, tracked tasks internally, and did not delegate.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced a child lifecycle boundary late in the run; serial avoided child ownership boundaries altogether.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel gave each child a detailed prompt describing the existing package state, environment constraints, no-src-modification boundary, and specific deliverables.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all context local and verified version/spec alignment before writing the workspace.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No missing or conflicting child contract explains task success; the meaningful boundary was lifecycle timing after otherwise concrete delegation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel fetched ydata-profiling 4.16.1, copied source into /workspace, patched missing htmlmin support with minify_html, and wrote packaging metadata.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified v4.17.0 as matching the prompt dependencies, copied that source, and wrote matching metadata and supporting files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: They used different upstream versions and setup details, but both produced source trees accepted by the official tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel launched child work but the parent received an AgentSwarm result showing both child agents aborted after the active turn was canceled.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial reached a normal final response summarizing the project layout, tests, issue tests, and wheel verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost the child-result lifecycle and final reporting step; serial completed its local result lifecycle.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel saved a shared workspace containing parent source files plus child-generated tests, docs, root config, and examples.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial saved a coherent workspace with source, build/lib copies, official tests/data, and a small example set.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared state did not show a write collision; its extra files came from child direct writes, while serial build artifacts came from its wheel/build path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent completed smoke/CLI checks and child agent-0 iterated tests, but the child final pytest command was interrupted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran upstream unit tests, issue regression tests, targeted workspace tests, CLI checks, and wheel package-data verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial had cleaner closure evidence; parallel had enough artifact quality for official pass but left a child verification command unfinished.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the full cell budget, timed out, and had no completed prompt event despite a passing official artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished in 966 seconds, did not time out, and had a completed prompt event with substantial remaining budget.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The official outcome matched, but parallel closure was materially worse because the child swarm was interrupted at the budget boundary.

outcome_analysis.explanation: There is no discordant official outcome: both current completed status evaluations report solution_passed true with reward 1.0. The concrete task-solving difference is process and artifact shape, not pass/fail: parallel implemented and smoke-tested the package then launched children for tests and scaffolding but timed out before those children returned; serial handled the entire path locally, ran larger upstream verification, and completed its final summary.
parallel_contributors: Parent-created source tree, minify fallback patch, editable install, smoke tests, and child-generated tests/docs/examples produced an accepted artifact.
The late AgentSwarm cancellation degraded closure evidence but did not prevent official pass.
serial_contributors: The single actor selected v4.17.0 from dependency-pin evidence and kept source, packaging, tests, and final report in one lifecycle.
The serial run ran upstream unit and issue tests plus a wheel check before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used ydata-profiling 4.16.1 and generated a custom test/docs/examples scaffold; serial used v4.17.0 and copied official tests/data.
Parallel missed some child-assigned feature example scripts after cancellation, but the official evaluator did not require them for pass.
evaluator_effects: The official evaluator scored the saved artifact after a parallel process timeout, so process_ok false did not change solution_passed.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is an adverse parallel process event only

There were not separately implemented incompatible components awaiting an unassigned integrator; the source tree was already integrated by the parent.
The parent wrote packaging files and assembled an installable workspace; missing child final reports are a lifecycle issue, not unowned assembly.
The parent owned source setup, install, smoke verification, delegation, and artifact delivery; the observed problem is terminal cancellation.
The parent did source implementation and smoke checks rather than blocking all productive work behind a mandatory preflight gate.
The child agents were implementers for tests and scaffolding, not a completed investigation-only phase delaying later implementation.
No indispensable implementation path is shown starved by auxiliary work; core source and package verification were already completed.
Only two children were launched, so the timeout is not directly caused by excessive breadth or repeated fan-out retries.
Agent-1's broad scaffolding scope is a near match, but the same chain is directly evidenced as active cancellation before child return.
The child prompts included environment constraints, no-source-modification boundaries, deliverables, and verification expectations.
The delegated scopes were disjoint tests versus docs/examples/scaffolding, and no incompatible cross-agent interface emerged.
No known finding or current-file fact is shown omitted during transfer and then repeated or misused by a receiver.
The delegated prompts were long but usable; the adverse event was cancellation, not receiver inability to reduce returned information.
No child or parent consumed a handoff describing superseded workspace or requirement state before acting.
No incompatible returned reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated.
The parallel parent did not make an observable whole-task completion decision; it timed out after child cancellation.
There was no replacement or retry child repeating prior work without inherited findings or workspace state.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The parent launched two active child agents and the orchestration canceled the active turn before either child returned a completed result, leaving final child summaries and final parent reporting absent.
candidates.realized_consequence: Both child results were aborted before final return, the parent had prompt_outcome.success false, and final reporting/child verification were cut off although the official artifact passed.
candidates.near_match_reason: No Failure Takeover is downstream of the same cancellation chain; the raw event is an active child interruption, not a completed child failure followed by an ignored takeover decision.

candidates.reason: The workspace itself was already captured and passed; this is not a complete candidate left unpromoted or unpackaged.
The child changes were mostly tests, docs, and examples; no required implementation change was integrated after a relevant final acceptance check.
The children wrote directly to the shared workspace and did not complete retrievable implementation results that the parent failed to join.
Agent-0's verifier-like pytest run was interrupted and did not produce a concrete completed finding trapped below the parent.
The child aborts belong to the retained Early Child Termination episode; no separate parent decision to ignore a failed child is visible.
No completed child result was available to the parent and then ignored; the AgentSwarm returned aborted children.
The parent waited on AgentSwarm, but the directly evidenced boundary is active cancellation rather than ignoring available progress until timeout.
The children worked on disjoint test versus docs/example scopes; no competing implementation designs required reconciliation.
No live agents are shown editing the same file and observing or reconciling concurrent same-file changes.
No non-entry source module produced by one agent was replaced or wholesale rewritten by another live agent.
No required executable, entry-point source, or submitted artifact was replaced while another agent owned it.
No broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replaced multiple current outputs and invalidated another agent's final-tree work.
Although agents wrote a shared workspace, the evidence does not show an unstable-state or provenance problem from unisolated writes.
No generated cache, fixture, temp path, tool output, or auxiliary implementation from one actor was consumed by another as stable reference input.
